newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-KPN says trading probe no problem.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-KPN says trading probe no problem.

text.p: The head of Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) said the Dutch postal and telecommunications giant was ready to cooperate with Australian regulators into unusual options trading in target company TNT Ltd.

Wim Dik, chairman and chief executive of KPN, also said in a television interview that the investigation by the Australian Securities Commission (ASC) had not tainted KPN's friendly A$2.0 billion bid for the transport and logistics firm.
The ASC won court approval on Friday to freeze about A$10 million in profits from TNT options trading which occurred just before the bid was announced last Wednesday.
"Somebody has been very stupid," Dik said of the trading in TNT options which had been virtually worthless until KPN unveiled its A$2.45 per share cash bid.
"If that somebody is found he has a problem," he said. "If the Australian Securities Commission will ask us to cooperate we will do (so), TNT will (also) do (so) by all means.
"And I don't think it has any influence over the deal at all," he told the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.
The KPN chief said the takeover talks had been a closely guarded secret on both sides, quite an achievement in Australia where media leaks about corporate deals are common.

Dik said KPN made a generous offer for TNT because it was worth the money, and because KPN wanted the board to immediately approve the bid to its shareholders rather than potentially face a long delay with a lower starting bid that had to be constantly increased.
The KPN offer was 50 percent or 81 cents per share above TNT's closing price the day before the takeover was announced.
Dik said while he had been told by people in Australia that he "must be stupid to pay so much", KPN based its offer on TNT's attractive operations in Europe which were above-average standard.
